rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Read the current body this session (line-by-line, plus a fresh grep of the 40 this/that/these/those/This/That spans over curriculum/evals/body-views/....body.txt). Closest-to-violating candidates, each resolves inside its own chunk: chunk 4 line 44 'This is a hard evolution from Cognition's 2025 Don't Build Multi-Agents stance' — 'This' points at the verbatim architectural claim quoted the sentence before, same chunk. Chunk 5 line 62 'Amp changed its mind about the whole mechanism' — 'the whole mechanism' resolves to Handoff, named at lines 56/58/60 earlier in the same chunk. Chunk 8 line 128 'The dispatcher pattern scales cross-repo' — resolves to the 'CLAUDE.md routing' bullet (line 112) and 'CLAUDE.md as half the system' bullet (line 126), both earlier in the same chunk. Chunk 6 line 83 'Cherny does not publish a unified framework over these moves' — 'these moves' resolves to the bulleted list opening the same chunk (lines 75-81). No never-named or forward-pointing referent found anywhere in the file.

Ran this session: grep -niE "the opening lecture|earlier module|previous module|this module said|as we saw|as covered|as discussed above|the last (module|lecture|exercise)" over the body projection -> 0 matches (exit 1). No chunk locates another file by position. Chunk 6 line 88 'the moves listed above' is a within-file sequential callback to the same chunk's own bullet list (permitted by rule 1); re-confirmed live this session via `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file <this file> --report` -> 'ok ...workflow-composition-lineages.md:88 [moves listed above] — maintainer-attested', matching the maintainer block's accept-note (current line 149). External docs are named by title throughout (chunk 2 line 24, chunk 8 line 133), never located by page position.

Every chunk (1-9) carries a self-sufficient claim beyond a bare wait-state. Closest-to-thin: chunk 1 (lines 5-14), three short numbered reading rules — each states a complete, standalone instruction, not a fragment dependent on neighbouring slides.

Every header previews what its chunk delivers under the sequential read. Chunk 5's header names both artefacts the chunk covers (Feedback Loopable, Handoff) and line 56 ('Amp published twice here, with different bylines and different shapes') confirms the two-part structure. Chunk 9's header 'How to pick what to study' is answered exactly by the three numbered filters that follow the (now count-free) lede 'Filters that work better than ranking:' (line 137) — dropping the word 'Three' from that lede, the only body change since the prior slides pass, makes the header's claim safer, not weaker: the header no longer implies a count the reader must verify against the list. No header contradicted by its own content.

Ran this session: grep -n "Not .*\. Not .*\." over the body projection -> 0 matches (exit 1). Self-grading superlative check: grep -niE "one of the (most|best)|the most (useful|important|valuable)|best-in-class|game.chang" -> 0 matches; line 81 'The single tip Cherny names as most important' attributes the superlative to Cherny's own ranking of his own tip, not a self-grading claim about this curriculum's value — not the banned value-prop leak. Number+retraction check: grep -niE "could be more|could be less|roughly|about [0-9]" -> only line 46's 'roughly 58%', sitting inside a verbatim attributed Yan quote, not an authored hedge (the banned shape is an authored 'about 10%... could be more, could be less', not a cited stat). Anaphora check: chunk 9 lines 139-143's four 'If you're.../If your team...' clauses each map a distinct scenario to a distinct named practitioner (Klaassen/Pocock/Yan-Cognition/Metcalf-Amp) — an enumerated lookup, not a hollow rhetorical triple with an empty final leg. No abstraction-noun stacks or empty-leg verb triplets found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Bold-span inventory this session (grep -noE '\*\*[^*]+\*\*' over the body projection, cross-checked against lines 104-146 of the current file — unchanged from the prior pass, the file's only edit since sits at line 137, outside these chunks): chunk 8 (Skill stacking, lines 104-134) carries eight content-bold spans on one slide — seven bulleted leads (line 117 'A single orchestrator', 118 'Phase-organised skill catalogue.', 119 'Design principles', 123 'Front-loaded read-only analysis.', 124 'Mandatory gates fire positionally', 125 'Re-invocation as control flow.', 126 'CLAUDE.md as half the system.') plus one inline handle (line 128 'scales cross-repo'). None is a §34 task-sizing callout, a module-template LO bullet, or content on a reading-list/menu/lookup surface (this is a narrative worked-example section, not a scanned list) — the per-slide COUNT is the pre-2026-07-09 monoculture the rule bans. Chunk 9 (How to pick what to study, lines 135-146): three bold spans (line 139 'What shape is your real work?' — 6 words; line 141 'How much orchestration do you want to author?' — 8 words; line 143 'What review bandwidth do you have?' — 6 words) each bold the FULL question of its filter entry, exceeding the ≲5-word handle cap; none is a coined term or named law. Considered and rejected as a covered reading-list/menu waiver: that waiver lifts the per-slide COUNT but explicitly keeps the handle-length cap, and names this exact failure ('Bolding mode-plus-title is the pre-2026-07-09 monoculture wearing a list for cover') — here the whole question is bolded with the answer prose left plain, i.e. mode-plus-title with no plain title at all. Harm: on a slide carrying no size accept-note that would exempt it, three consecutive full-sentence bolds flatten the bold signal into noise — a reader scanning for the slide's one handle finds three, none a named concept, while the actual navigational cue (which practitioner to read) sits in plain prose at the end of each entry. Unchanged from the prior slides pass (@e11bbeb4 body, now @3cc5c557 body); still un-actioned per standing orchestrator instruction — re-confirmed live rather than carried forward blind.
